keep.reason: Without it a reader would use 0o755 (matching a sibling writer); that exposes the ingest token embedded in the script to every other account on the machine.
Without it a reader would delete this defer; that leaves tmpPath on disk if rename fails.
Without it a reader would delete the Sync() call; that breaks durability because a crash between Sync and Rename loses the write despite the rename itself being atomic.
Without it a reader would remove the `dir` parameter to simplify the signature; that breaks test fixtures that set this field directly.
Without it a reader would change to os.WriteFile; that allows torn writes when two different sessions launch into the same directory and race on settings.local.json.

Without it a reader would remove generation and just reset the maps on identity change; that allows a stale check result started under the old identity to cache if it lands after the identity changes.

Without it a reader might use ctx directly in the shared run instead of context.WithoutCancel(ctx); that allows a leader's cancelled request to cancel the run and break concurrent callers waiting on the same result.
Without it a reader would unconditionally delete f.inflight[model]; that deletes a newer generation's call out from under its own waiters when an identity changes mid-check.
Without it a reader would duplicate the %q formatting in both launchError and models response; that allows the two messages to drift.
Without it a reader might construct a second cache for the launcher's pre-check instead of passing the same one; that violates the 'exactly one cache owner' constraint.
Without it a reader might set message for other verdicts like 'unchecked' or 'recognized'; that violates the Protocol Contract: message is present iff verdict is unrecognized.
Without it a reader would skip the generation check before passing appliedToCurrentStore; that applies focus from a stale refusal that landed after the dialog was cancelled and reopened.
Without it a reader would duplicate the preset list in launch.ts or index.html; that allows the DOM and code to drift.
Without it a reader would call resetVerdictStore per-verdict-request instead of per-open; that resets generation and drops concurrent verdict requests.
